reason: Cell junctions appear to join neighboring surface cells, a useful first step in building a protective skin layer.
expectation: The junctions will connect the surface cells into a sheet.

effect: The junctions joined the surface cells into a sheet, so I can continue building the skin layers.
reaction: The tug illustration makes the junctions’ role clear.
reason: The tough outer layer looks suited to covering the connected surface cells and adding protection.
expectation: The outer layer will cover the connected cells to form a more protective surface.

effect: The connected cells and outer layer formed a surface barrier; the living cells beneath replace the dead outer cells.
reaction: The distinction between the living and outer layers is clear.
reason: The support cells and connective fibers appear to belong together in the supporting layer of skin.
expectation: They will form a supportive tissue for the skin.

effect: The support cells and collagen fibers formed a supporting skin layer with capillaries, ready to join the surface barrier.
reaction: The tug panels clarify how the fibers contribute support.
reason: The supporting layer and surface barrier appear to be the two layers needed to build the skin.
expectation: The layers will join into a protective skin structure.

effect: The layers formed skin, and the picture shows oxygen and nutrients reaching the living surface cells from vessels below.
reaction: The cross-section clearly connects the skin layers to their supply.
reason: The skin still needs sensory endings to detect contact.
expectation: The nerve endings will make the layered skin able to sense touch.

effect: The sensory endings completed the protective, touch-sensitive skin. The next goal is to connect it and the supply network to the arm.
reaction: The contact arrows make the sensory role clear.
reason: The arm needs the sensitive skin as its protective covering.
expectation: The skin will cover the arm and add touch sensing.

effect: The skin now covers the arm and connects to its nerves; the open vessels show where the supply network belongs.
reaction: The open vessel ends make the next connection clear.
reason: The arm needs its vessels connected to the body supply network for continuing supplies.
expectation: The network will connect to the arm’s vessels and supply its tissues.

effect: The supply network connected to the arm, creating a living body model. The next goal is to interact with the glass.
reaction: The upper-body cutaway brings the connected systems together.
reason: The body model and glass are the visible pieces needed to lift the glass.
expectation: The model will lift the glass, setting up the slipping contact.

effect: The body lifted the glass, which is beginning to slip; changing fingertip contact is now needed to steady it.
reaction: The downward arrow makes the problem clear.
reason: Changing fingertip contact is the remaining cue for detecting the slip and adjusting the grip.
expectation: The contact information will help the hand adjust its grip and steady the glass.

effect: Changing fingertip contact completed the feedback loop: sensory signals help the hand muscles adjust their grip and steady the glass.
reaction: The sequence from slipping to a firmer grip is satisfying and makes the roles of touch and muscle work clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Steadying the slipping glass brought the chapter’s skin, nerves, and muscles together in a concrete example. The three panels and signal pathway explain why holding still requires active work.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the surface layer was straightforward, but the two successive combinations felt somewhat predictable before the skin was connected to the rest of the body.

surprise.text: The outermost skin cells being dead, while living layers below replace them, added a useful distinction to the protective barrier.

arbitrary.text: Changing fingertip contact was an unusual object to combine, though its picture and the goal made its purpose clear.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it used another everyday action to connect the body systems. The glass example gave the earlier construction a clear purpose.
